title: ResISC: Residue Number System-Based Integrated Sensing and Computing for Efficient Edge AI
problem: Edge AI on power-constrained devices requires efficient sensing and processing; conventional image processing and CNN inference consume significant power; integrated sensing-computing can reduce data movement but requires novel processing paradigms.
motivation: Edge AI applications in IoT, robotics, and surveillance need extreme power efficiency; processing-near-sensor architectures can reduce power by eliminating data movement, but require new number systems and encoding strategies.
method: ResISC uses residue number system (RNS) for efficient computation: in-sensor residue encoder converts images directly to RNS in analog domain, RNS-based CNN accelerator processes RNS data using SOT-MRAM cells, and mixed-radix unit performs efficient RNS activation operations. Selective channel deactivation reduces overhead.
key_novelty: First integrated sensing-computing architecture using residue number system for both analog image encoding and RNS-based digital CNN processing.
contributions: In-sensor RNS encoder converting images to residue domain in analog domain
RNS-based CNN accelerator using SOT-MRAM for energy-efficient computation
Mixed-radix unit for efficient RNS activation operations
Selective channel deactivation reducing computation by up to 89%, 3.4x power efficiency gain, 71x execution time reduction
Competitive accuracy (up to 94.63% on CIFAR-10) with minimal degradation
primary_theme: Residue number system-based in-sensor CNN processing
